claim: Atg4 removes the residue(s) C-terminal to Gly116 of Atg8, exposing glycine

context: S. cerevisiae, in vivo + in vitro
confidence: high; reference organism, not N. crassa

claim: Exposed C-terminal Gly is the PE acceptor; Atg7 E1 and Atg3 E2 required
finding: Amide bond between Atg8 C-terminal Gly and PE amino group; Atg7->Atg3 route
confidence: high; defines the feature set tested

claim: Two hydrophobic pockets of Atg8 capture Trp and Leu of a WxxL AIM
finding: 15 Atg8 residues contact the Atg19 WEEL peptide; HP1 and HP2 defined
confidence: high; source of the contact set

claim: APG-6 has Gly at the Atg4-exposed position with a cleavable extension
finding: 78.6% id to yeast Atg8; Gly116 aligns 1:1; 110-SGENTFG-116 identical; 117-DFETA-121 propeptide
confidence: high for the residue call; cannot prove cleavage occurs

claim: AIM-docking surface is conserved in APG-6
finding: 15/15 AIM contacts identical (13/13 pocket-lining); 100% vs 78.6% background, binomial p=0.027
confidence: high conservation; no measured APG-6 interaction

claim: N. crassa encodes the enzymes the cycle needs

claim: Autophagic structures form in N. crassa
